turns.result:
The test deal went through: the payment was **Released** to the seller in 61 seconds. It ran on Sepolia, a public test network, with tUSDC test tokens, so no real money moved.

- **Who sold:** Crow's test seller (https://escrow.stream/agents/test-seller), offering from address `0x143688…f4dc`. Your agent was the buyer, using fresh keys (`0xd5c5ca…3af6`) that existed only in memory.
- **The deal:** 3 rows of `customer_id,email` for 25 tUSDC, 30.71 tUSDC in all. 26 tUSDC was held (the price plus a 1 tUSDC adjudication fee), and a 4.71 tUSDC operator fee was paid on top.
- **Outcome:** all three checks the deal used passed (the columns, exactly 3 rows, and no duplicate rows), and the adjudicator accepted. The buyer decrypted its copy, confirmed it matched the delivered file, and got `1,ada@example.com | 2,alan@example.com | 3,grace@example.com`.
- **Commitment ID:** `0xc5be624d16df9248f21175e79e5ee667f31cfbb149a386183105ece97793de52`. It became final at 13:43:00 UTC, when the 60-second appeal window closed.
- **Sepolia transactions:**
  - Funded: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0x9186a2eba72fa4b83cdf7e33e1cc1d97dca1992862185f4dd14e72d50f912af9
  - Delivered: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0x5f30f80a82a90b49785ffbdcdb3fd193dc34408600085272a946d5061db3c9c8
  - Decided: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0x058c7e1df116a42276257b38688bf73bad1ce87ae0f0ef7c4c9e1bbee4657d7d

The script and its two packages are in `crow-try/`. To try the refund path, add `--outcome refund` to the end of the command: the price comes back, but the two fees don't. The test seller allows only 3 requests per IP address an hour.
